body.statement: Theorem 1. On the explicit union \[\{(2,(1,-1)),(2,(-1,1))\}\cup\{(K,c):K\ge3,\ c\in\mathcal C_K\},\] the unrestricted risk satisfies \[R_n(c)=n^{-1}-C_AV_c(s_c/2)^{2/3}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}),\qquad \lim_{n\to\infty}n^{4/3}d_n(c)=\Lambda_c.\] On the at-least-three-active-arm component, the independent allocation \(q^\star\) and the total full-label nonlinear Airy estimator attain the expansion. On the published two-arm component, the two-arm reduction proposition gives \(V_c(s_c/2)=1\) and recovers Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026), Theorem 3.1. Thus the union contains the published two-arm class as its first component and adds every fixed normalized contrast with at least three active arms as its second component, with the two-arm reduction providing the bridge.
body.justification: The equality identifies both the universal Airy law and the contrast-specific response-alphabet curvature in the unrestricted multi-arm game.
body.gap: The closest sharp theorem is the two-arm expansion of Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026); no searched source gives a multi-arm response-alphabet coefficient or an all-face lower bound.
body.consumer: For an ACTG-175-style four-regimen binary trial, the theorem determines whether the prespecified regimen-versus-average allocation and nonlinear shrinkage rule are second-order minimax.
